analysis.title: Market Musings 11/26: Too big to ignore
key_insights: A standard MSCI country index covers only the large- and mid-cap segments, designed to capture about 85% of a country's free-float-adjusted market capitalisation. The next 14% is the small-cap universe, which sits outside the standard index.
Size thresholds for large, mid and small cap differ by country, so the definition of small cap also varies across MSCI regional indices.

At the end of August 2026 the largest constituent of the MSCI USA Small Cap Index was about USD 30 billion, excluding Moderna, which the report treats as an outlier. The largest constituent of the MSCI Germany Small Cap Index was EUR 9.7 billion. US small caps are generally larger than European ones.
The largest company in the MSCI World Small Cap Index was about US$3 billion 20 years ago and is closer to US$30 billion now.
Aggregate revenues of MSCI World Small Cap constituents were 20% of MSCI World Large Cap revenues in 2006 and about 28% in 2026. The chart shows 23% for 2016.

Small caps account for around 75% of listed companies in the United States and over 60% in Germany. Many are niche leaders in specialised industrial and technology markets that are underrepresented in large caps.

The author concludes that investors limited to standard MSCI indices miss a large and growing part of the equity market, and that adding small caps widens the range of companies, industries and sources of growth.
risk_factors: The disclaimer states that small-cap equities can be more volatile and less liquid than mid- and large-cap equities.
The disclaimer lists country risk, equity market risk and small-cap company risk as risks of small-cap strategies, which can rise significantly under unusual market conditions.
charts_described: Chart 1 plots the largest market cap in the MSCI World Small Cap Index, excluding Sandisk, at 3.2bn (2006), 8.9bn (2016) and 29.9bn (2026, H126 end), in US$bn.
Chart 1 also plots small-cap index revenues as a percentage of large-cap index revenues at 20% (2006), 23% (2016) and 28% (2026).

theme_stances.key_argument: Standard MSCI indices omit a large and increasingly important part of the equity market, and small caps offer access to a wider range of companies, industries and sources of growth.
theme_stances.evidence: It's an opportunity set that is simply too big to ignore.
